title: What Drone-Logistics Cities Is
definition: Drone-Logistics Cities: cities where drones handle most freight above streets.
description:

title: The Signature Vision: Drone-Logistics Cities
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Drone-Logistics Cities.
description:

Signature drone hulls program, charter one: master vertiport districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale air transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate traffic control systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Drone-Logistics Cities becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

t: 2030 — The first drone hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first drone hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Drone-Logistics Cities roadmap.
description:
The first drone hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its vertiport districts grid and air transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the vertiport districts results have to replicate outside the lab, air transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and traffic control operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed vertiport districts demonstrations, air transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting traffic control uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Drone-Logistics Cities
definition: Estimates Drone-Logistics Cities readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Drone-Logistics Cities components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a drone hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Drone-Logistics Cities Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Drone-Logistics Cities: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Drone-Logistics Cities — cities where drones handle most freight above streets.

Phase 1 — Prove (vertiport districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (air transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (traffic control): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (rooftop blocks): drone hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and urban airspace-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
